title: From Sorting Cans to Speaking Up: The Real Rewards of Volunteering
title_zh: 从分拣罐头到敢于发言：做志愿者的真正收获
intro_zh: 本文约 559 词，难度适合 CET-4。文章从沟通、同理心、韧性、主动性、视角和感恩等方面，介绍做志愿者带来的真实收获。

paragraphs.en: Many people think volunteering is a one-way gift: you give your time, and someone else receives help. But ask anyone who has spent a few months at a food bank or animal shelter, and you will hear a different story. They often say they got more than they gave. Research shows that regular volunteers report higher happiness and life satisfaction. The real rewards are skills and insights that last.
paragraphs.zh: 很多人认为做志愿者是单向的付出：你付出时间，别人得到帮助。但问问任何在食物银行或动物收容所待过几个月的人，你会听到不同的故事。他们常说得到的比付出的更多。研究表明，定期做志愿者的人报告更高的幸福感和生活满意度。真正的回报是持久的技能和见解。

paragraphs.en: One of the first things you learn is communication. At a food bank, volunteers must talk to people from all walks of life. Some are shy; others are angry or worried. You learn to listen without judging and explain things clearly. A volunteer named Maria said that after six months of sorting cans and talking to visitors, she became much more confident. This kind of commitment to showing up every week also builds trust.
paragraphs.zh: 你最先学到的事情之一是沟通。例如，在食物银行，志愿者必须与来自各行各业的人交谈。有些人害羞；有些人愤怒或担忧。你学会不加评判地倾听，并清晰地解释事情。一位名叫玛丽亚的志愿者说，在分拣罐头和与来访者交谈六个月后，她变得自信多了。这种每周都出现的承诺也建立起了信任。

paragraphs.en: Another gain is empathy. When you spend time with elderly people in a nursing home or children in a hospital, you begin to see the world through their eyes. You notice small details: a shaky hand, a forced smile, a quiet sigh. This deeper understanding changes how you treat everyone, not just those you help. It makes you kinder and more patient, even when you feel tired yourself.
paragraphs.zh: 另一个收获是同理心。当你花时间陪伴养老院的老人或医院的儿童时，你开始通过他们的眼睛看世界。你注意到小细节：颤抖的手、勉强的微笑、无声的叹息。这种更深的理解改变了你对待每个人的方式，而不仅仅是你帮助的人。它让你更善良、更有耐心，即使在你感到疲惫的时候。

paragraphs.en: Volunteering also builds resilience. Things rarely go as planned. A charity run may face heavy rain; a donation drive may collect far less than expected. Instead of giving up, you learn to adjust, ask for help, and try again. One student volunteer described how her team reorganized a book sale three times in one weekend. By Sunday evening, they had raised $1,200. Failure is just a step.
paragraphs.zh: 做志愿者也能培养韧性。事情很少按计划进行。一场慈善长跑可能遇到大雨；一次捐赠活动可能筹到的物资远低于预期。你没有放弃，而是学会调整、寻求帮助并再次尝试。一位学生志愿者描述她的团队在一个周末内三次重新组织图书义卖。到周日晚上，他们筹到了 1200 美元。失败只是其中一步。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps the most surprising reward is initiative. In a paid job, someone often tells you what to do. In volunteering, you must spot problems and act. If the shelves are messy, you organize them. If a new person looks lost, you offer a tour. This freedom can feel scary at first, but it quickly builds confidence. Employers love this quality on a resume; it shows you can lead.
paragraphs.zh: 也许最令人惊讶的回报是主动性。在有薪工作中，通常有人告诉你该做什么。在做志愿者时，你必须发现问题并采取行动。如果架子乱了，你就整理它们。如果新来的人看起来迷路了，你就主动带他们参观。这种自由起初可能令人害怕，但很快就能建立信心。雇主喜欢简历上的这种品质；它表明你能领导。

paragraphs.en: Volunteering also gives you a new perspective. You meet people whose lives are very different from yours. A retired teacher may share stories of growing up without electricity. A refugee may describe leaving everything behind. These conversations make your own problems seem smaller. You stop complaining about slow Wi-Fi and start appreciating a warm meal. This shift in thinking is one of the most lasting gifts of service.
paragraphs.zh: 做志愿者还给你一个新的视角。你会遇到与你生活截然不同的人。一位退休教师可能分享在没有电的环境中长大的故事。一位难民可能描述抛弃一切的经历。这些对话让你自己的问题显得更小。你不再抱怨网速慢，而是开始感激一顿热饭。这种思维转变是服务带来的最持久的礼物之一。

paragraphs.en: There is also a practical side. Studies show that volunteers are more likely to find jobs because they develop teamwork and time-management skills. A 2022 survey of 500 hiring managers found that 65% preferred candidates with volunteer experience. And the feeling of gratitude you receive from others can boost your mental health. One volunteer said, 'When a child smiles and says thank you, I forget how tired I am.' That emotional reward is hard to measure but hard to ignore.
paragraphs.zh: 还有实际的一面。研究表明，志愿者更有可能找到工作，因为他们培养了团队合作和时间管理技能。2022 年一项针对 500 名招聘经理的调查发现，65% 的人更青睐有志愿者经历的候选人。而你从他人那里得到的感激可以提升你的心理健康。一位志愿者说：“当一个孩子微笑着感谢我时，我就忘了自己有多累。”这种情感回报很难衡量，也很难忽视。

paragraphs.en: So volunteering is not just about helping others. It is a two-way street where you gain skills, friends, and a stronger sense of purpose. You do not need to commit every weekend. Even two hours a month can make a difference—for the community and for you. The next time you see a sign asking for volunteers, why not say yes? You may be surprised by what you get.
paragraphs.zh: 所以做志愿者不仅仅是帮助他人。这是一条双向街，你获得技能、朋友和更强的目标感。你不必每个周末都投入。即使每月两小时也能带来改变——对社区和你自己。下次你看到招募志愿者的告示时，为什么不答应呢？你可能会惊讶于自己得到的回报。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Volunteering is a one-way gift that only helps others.
Volunteering brings unexpected rewards to the volunteers themselves.
Volunteering should be done every weekend to be effective.
Volunteering is mainly a way to find a paid job.
questions.explain: 文章开篇就指出做志愿者并非单向付出，接着从沟通、同理心、韧性、主动性、视角和感恩等方面说明志愿者自身的收获。因此主旨是志愿者工作给志愿者带来意想不到的回报。

questions.q: According to the passage, how does volunteering help build communication skills?
options: By talking to people from different backgrounds.
By writing reports for charity organizations.
By using social media to share stories.
questions.explain: 第二段提到，在食物银行，志愿者必须与来自各行各业的人交谈，并学会不加评判地倾听和清晰地解释，从而提升沟通能力。选项 B 与原文一致。

questions.q: What can be inferred about resilience from the passage?
options: Volunteers should avoid challenges to stay calm.
Volunteers learn to adapt when things do not go as planned.
Resilience is only useful for finding a job.
Resilience means never asking for help.
questions.explain: 第四段说明志愿者工作很少一帆风顺，志愿者学会调整、寻求帮助并再次尝试，还举了图书义卖的例子。这说明韧性是在遇到困难时学会适应和坚持。选项 B 符合推断。

questions.q: What does the word 'perspective' in Paragraph 6 most probably mean?
options: A way of thinking about things.
questions.explain: 第六段中，perspective 指通过接触不同生活背景的人，志愿者获得看待世界的新角度。后文提到这些对话让志愿者不再抱怨小事，开始感激生活。因此 perspective 意为“看待事物的方式”，选项 A 正确。
